questions.learningObjective: evaluate type hierarchy in a design critique
questions.stem: On Type hierarchy: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that every heading on a page uses the same size and weight. What is the main problem this creates for readers?

options.text: The page has too much white space between the headings
options.misconception: blames empty space for a lack of rank among the headings

options.text: All of the headings should be set in italic instead
options.misconception: mistakes a change of style for a real hierarchical difference

options.text: The body text is too short to justify having any headings
options.misconception: misidentifies the issue as an amount of content

options.text: No level stands out so readers cannot scan the structure

questions.explanation: Visual hierarchy uses differences in size, weight, and position to show the relative importance of elements. When all headings look alike the structure of the page is invisible, and readers cannot scan or grasp what is most important.
questions.hint: How would a reader tell a main topic from one of its subheadings?
